label: Indonesia: Borneo, Sulawesi, Raja Ampat · Jan 16
title: Borneo, North Sulawesi & Raja Ampat: orangutans by houseboat, tarsiers, muck diving, the world's richest reefs and Waigeo at night
summary: Tanjung Puting by houseboat (orangutans, proboscis monkeys), Tangkoko (tarsiers, macaques, cuscus), Lembeh muck diving (6 dives), Raja Ampat (10 dives, mantas) and Waigeo night walks. ~$4,423 pp.
overview:
- **Built around reptiles, amphibians, mammals and fish** (birds are a bonus): apes and monkeys in Borneo, primates and marsupials in Sulawesi, critters and big reef fish underwater, night walks for cuscus, frogs and snakes on Waigeo.
- **Dates:** LAX Sat Dec 26 → LAX Sat Jan 16. 20 nights on the ground (plus 1 on a plane).
- **Route:** Jakarta 1n → **Tanjung Puting 2n** (houseboat) → Jakarta 1n → **Tangkoko 2n** → **Lembeh Strait 3n** (6 muck dives) → ✈ direct to Sorong 1n → **Arborek 6n** (10 dives, mantas) → **Waigeo 3n** (treks, two night walks, Kali Biru) → Jakarta 1n.
- **Borneo:** three days on a private klotok up the Sekonyer River: orangutans at Camp Leakey, proboscis monkeys roosting along the river at dusk, gibbons calling, crocodiles by spotlight.
- **Two kinds of diving:** Lembeh is the world capital of muck diving (frogfish, mimic octopus, flamboyant cuttlefish, mandarinfish). The Dampier Strait has the highest reef-fish and coral diversity recorded anywhere (mantas, sharks, big schools). You're Advanced Open Water, so the current sites and deeper pinnacles are open to you.
- **To fit Jan 16,** the Piaynemo viewpoint day was dropped rather than any dives (16 dives in total).
- **Budget: ~$4,423 pp**, including ~5% contingency.

itinerary.title: Fly toward Jakarta
itinerary.details: LAX → Jakarta (CGK) with one stop in Tokyo, Taipei or Seoul, ~22–24h. ANA showed ~$1,106 round trip for December 2026 dates.

itinerary.title: Land Jakarta late
itinerary.details: Arrive CGK in the evening (the date line eats a day). Airport hotel; sleep.

itinerary.title: Borneo: up the Sekonyer River by houseboat
itinerary.details: Early flight CGK → Pangkalan Bun (~1h20). The crew meets you and drives you 20 minutes to Kumai harbour, where you board a private klotok, a wooden houseboat with a crew, guide and cook. Cruise up the Sekonyer River into Tanjung Puting National Park, past long-tailed macaques and kingfishers. Afternoon at the Tanjung Harapan feeding station for orangutans. At dusk, proboscis monkeys settle into the riverside trees to sleep. You sleep on the top deck on mattresses under mosquito nets (no tent needed).

itinerary.title: Orangutans at Camp Leakey
itinerary.details: Morning at Pondok Tanggui, then upriver to Camp Leakey, the research camp Biruté Galdikas founded in 1971. Orangutans at the feeding platform and around camp, plus bearded pigs and gibbons calling in the forest. Afternoon forest trek with your guide. After dark, spotlight the river from the boat for crocodiles (the rare false gharial lives here) and watch fireflies in the riverside trees.

itinerary.title: Last forest walk, back to Jakarta
itinerary.details: Dawn on the river: proboscis monkeys and hornbills. A short jungle walk, then downriver to Kumai by midday. Afternoon flight Pangkalan Bun → Jakarta. Airport hotel.
itinerary.meals: B, L on board; D own

itinerary.title: To North Sulawesi; tarsiers at dusk
itinerary.details: Morning flight CGK → Manado (~3.5h; Manado is 1h ahead). Car to Batuputih at the edge of Tangkoko reserve (~2h). At dusk, a ranger takes you to a strangler fig where a family of spectral tarsiers — fist-sized primates with enormous eyes — wake up and leap off to hunt insects. New Year's Eve in Batuputih.

itinerary.title: Macaques, cuscus and a night walk
itinerary.details: Dawn walk with a ranger: troops of crested black macaques (critically endangered, unafraid of people) foraging on the forest floor, bear cuscus and Sulawesi dwarf cuscus in the canopy, flying lizards gliding between trunks. Rest through midday. Night walk: hunting tarsiers, Sulawesi pit vipers, frogs, sleeping birds and civets if lucky.

itinerary.title: Second dawn walk, then into the muck
itinerary.details: Second dawn walk for anything missed. Car to Bitung (~1.5h) and boat to a Lembeh dive resort. One afternoon dive to settle in on black volcanic sand.
itinerary.overnight: Budget dive resort, Lembeh Strait (full board)

itinerary.title: Muck diving: three dives
itinerary.details: Two day dives on Lembeh's black sand and rubble — frogfish, mimic and wonderpus octopus, flamboyant cuttlefish, ghost pipefish, pygmy seahorses, nudibranchs by the dozen — and a dusk dive for mating mandarinfish.
itinerary.overnight: Budget dive resort, Lembeh Strait (full board)

itinerary.title: Two last muck dives
itinerary.details: Two morning dives, then out of the water by midday to leave ~22h before tomorrow's flight. Afternoon off.
itinerary.overnight: Budget dive resort, Lembeh Strait (full board)

itinerary.title: Fly to West Papua
itinerary.details: Car to Manado airport (~1.5h). Direct flight Manado → Sorong (~1h25; Sorong is 1h ahead again). Buy all the cash (IDR) you'll need in Raja Ampat here — the islands have no reliable ATMs.

itinerary.title: Ferry into Raja Ampat
itinerary.details: 09:00 fast ferry Sorong → Waisai (~2h). Pay the Raja Ampat marine park tag and visitor levy at Waisai. Homestay boat to Arborek (~1h). Snorkel the Arborek jetty — schooling fish, wobbegong sharks under the pier — and look after dark for Raja Ampat's endemic 'walking' epaulette shark in the shallows.

itinerary.title: Dive day 1: check-out and Arborek reefs
itinerary.details: Two dives with Arborek Dive Shop (village-run): a check-out dive, then a Dampier Strait site. Afternoon snorkel.

itinerary.title: Dive day 2: Cape Kri and Sardine Reef
itinerary.details: Two dives on the strait's famous current sites — Cape Kri held the record for fish species counted on one dive. Strong currents; the guides pick the tide.

itinerary.title: Dive day 3: manta cleaning stations
itinerary.details: Two dives at Manta Sandy / Manta Ridge, where reef mantas queue at cleaning stations, plus a reef dive.

itinerary.title: Dive day 4: Blue Magic and Mioskon
itinerary.details: Two dives on pinnacles with big schools, sharks and pygmy seahorses — deeper sites your Advanced Open Water covers. Night snorkel off the jetty.

itinerary.title: Dive day 5: guides' choice
itinerary.details: Last two dives of the package at the guides' pick for the conditions.

itinerary.title: To Waigeo's rainforest; first night walk
itinerary.details: Homestay boat to Waigeo, Raja Ampat's biggest island (~1.5h). Afternoon forest walk with a village guide; monitor lizards on the forest edge. After dark, a night walk for the Waigeo spotted cuscus (found only on this island), northern common cuscus, fruit bats, frogs and snakes.

itinerary.title: The blue river
itinerary.details: Drive to Warsambin and trek ~1–1.5h through primary forest to Kali Biru, a river of clear blue water in the jungle — swim in it, look for skinks, frogs and freshwater fish. Second night walk on a different trail.

itinerary.title: Deep into the interior
itinerary.details: Full day on foot into unlogged lowland forest with a village guide: giant buttressed trees, lizards and frogs along the streams, hornbills and cockatoos overhead. Optional: the dawn red bird-of-paradise display before you set off.

itinerary.title: Back to Jakarta
itinerary.details: Car Saporkren → Waisai (~30m), 09:00 ferry to Sorong (~2h), afternoon flight Sorong → Jakarta (~4h). Airport hotel.

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: CGK → LAX with one stop; the date line gives the day back, so you land the same calendar day. Last dive was Jan 11.

practical:
## Entry
- **Indonesia:** e-Visa on Arrival, IDR 500k (~$32), 30 days. Official site only: evisa.imigrasi.go.id. Passport 6+ months, 2 blank pages.
- **Raja Ampat:** marine park tag (IDR 700k) + visitor levy (IDR 1M) ≈ IDR 1.7M, cash at Waisai. Carry the tag.
- **Lembeh:** small park entry (~IDR 100k) in cash.

## Money
- **Cash is everything.** Homestays, dive shops, boats and guides want IDR cash. Manado and Sorong have ATMs; Waisai's are unreliable and the islands have none.

## Packing
- **No camping gear needed.** Homestays are simple huts with a mattress and mosquito net, shared bathrooms (often a bucket 'mandi'), generator power in the evening.
- Your own mask, snorkel, fins and dive computer; a rash guard; reef-safe sunscreen; a dry bag.
- A strong headtorch (plus a red-light mode) for night walks and spotting eyeshine; binoculars; light long sleeves and trousers against mosquitoes; trail shoes that can get wet.
- Domestic flights allow ~20 kg checked; keep dive gear light.

## Health and safety
- **Malaria:** CDC lists all of West Papua (incl. Raja Ampat) as a risk area, and rural Sulawesi too — take prophylaxis (atovaquone-proguanil). Dengue too: DEET or picaridin day and night.
- **Diving:** strong currents in the Dampier Strait; dive with the local guides and a surface marker. Get dive accident cover — the nearest recompression chamber may be hours away.
- Medical care on the islands is minimal; evacuation cover is essential.
- Re-check the State Department's Indonesia advisory (it flags parts of the Papuan highlands, not Raja Ampat) before booking.

## Season
- Raja Ampat's diving season is roughly October–April; December–January brings showers and some northwest wind, but the Dampier Strait stays diveable.
- North Sulawesi is in its wet season (Dec–Jan): expect rain at Tangkoko; Lembeh diving runs year-round.
- Flying after diving: the plan leaves ~22h after the last Lembeh dive (Jan 4) and 4 days after the last Raja Ampat dive (Jan 11).
- Central Kalimantan is wet in Dec–Jan too; the klotok has a roof, and the river trips run year-round.

fatigue_check:
Long-haul both ends (~22–24h). Five domestic flights: Jakarta ⇄ Pangkalan Bun, Jakarta → Manado, Manado → Sorong, Sorong → Jakarta (all ≤4h).
Dec 31 (flight + 2h car) and Jan 15 (car, ferry, 4h flight) are the long days; Dec 28 and Dec 30 are short flights plus a river cruise.
No pure rest day: Borneo, Sulawesi and Raja Ampat run back to back, but most days are zero-transfer.
